items.title: Hello, I’m Ruoshui.
items.text: I’m a Computer Science student at the University of Toronto. I’m drawn to problems built around structure, rules, and reasoning — whether that means understanding why an algorithm works, tracing a bug through a system, or figuring out the structure of a language.

items.title: Education
items.text: University of Toronto · B.Sc., Computer Science Specialist and Classics (Greek and Latin) Major · Expected June 2029 · cGPA 4.0/4.0.

items.title: What I’m Exploring
items.text: I’m currently exploring theoretical and mathematically oriented computer science, especially algorithms, formal methods, and questions about how computational systems represent structure and rules.

items.title: Language & Computing
items.text: Alongside computer science, I study Ancient Greek and Latin. That has led me to an interest in computational linguistics, low-resource and historical languages, and questions about morphology, syntax, and systematic reasoning in language models.

items.title: Research
items.text: I’m interested in learning how to turn broad technical interests into precise research questions, and I hope to pursue research-focused graduate study in computer science in the future.

items.title: Teaching
items.text: At Kintore College, I regularly support peers and younger students with introductory programming and mathematics, especially proof strategies, problem decomposition, code tracing, and debugging.

items.title: Award
items.text: International Merit Admission Award, Faculty of Arts & Science · Recipient in 2025–26 and renewed for 2026–27.

items.title: Languages
items.text: Mandarin (native) · English (fluent) · Ancient Greek and Latin (academic study).

items.title: Interests
items.text: Algorithms · Theoretical computer science · Formal methods · Computational linguistics · Historical-language computing.

items.title: AACorn · Visual AAC Communication Board
items.text: Leading a team building an accessible Java application for pictogram-based communication. I work on the communication logic and help coordinate the project’s architecture, integration, and development.

items.title: Bird Species Interaction Network
items.text: Built and optimized the core weighted-graph algorithm in Python for a four-person project modelling seasonal bird co-occurrence from 6,000 real-world iNaturalist observations.

items.title: Team Cobalt · VR Game
items.text: Joined as Lead Developer / Technical Lead during the final development week, implementing and integrating core Unity/C# gameplay systems for a VR game exhibited at VRTO 2026.

items.title: Zhiyuan Robotics · Intern
items.text: Supported robotics testing and validation in Shanghai through test-set preparation, output review, and documentation of discrepancies for engineering follow-up.

items.title: Pattern Recognition Research
items.text: Worked on PCA- and SVM-based face-recognition experiments using Python, OpenCV, scikit-learn, and NumPy, with a focus on preprocessing and feature extraction.

items.title: Film Archive & Translation
items.text: Translate and technically edit bilingual subtitles for historical and international films, including timing, encoding, and quality control for releases reaching more than 30,000 downloads.
